Abu ~ Con + Pa
#mediator

fit4 <- sem(model4, data = dt_c, ordered= c("Con"), estimator = "WLSMV", group = "agresion_to_father")

messages.author: 08e48595b188026f
messages.subject: Re: Not getting robust fit indices for categorical path analysis and lavTestLRT not working: Help!
parts:
Hi,

The robust version of fit indicators for estimator DWLS and similar was introduced only with version 0.6-13 of lavaan. As it says there (https://www.lavaan.ugent.be/history/dot6.html) it computes robust fit indices only if ALL data are categorical. I think I read somewhere there is a work around (maybe search for it on this forum), but when I tried it (quite some time ago) I still didn't get the robust version.

As for multi group analysis. The output is simply saying that you have to report the scaled/robust chi-square (find in the model output) and not the chi-square that is reported as part of multigroup testing. The warning is because you are trying to compare models with the same degrees of freedom - which is not possible.
Related to the mutli group analysis. In Model 5, although you include Pa ~  Be you still have the same degrees of freedom because you are replacing Pa ~~  Be. For measurement invariance, you are trying to test equality of factor loadings which you don't have (path analysis).

Hope this helps.

Best,
Jošt

El lunes, 12 de febrero de 2024 a las 13:06:04 UTC-6, Jošt Bartol escribió:
Hi,

The robust version of fit indicators for estimator DWLS and similar was introduced only with version 0.6-13 of lavaan. As it says there (https://www.lavaan.ugent.be/history/dot6.html) it computes robust fit indices only if ALL data are categorical. I think I read somewhere there is a work around (maybe search for it on this forum), but when I tried it (quite some time ago) I still didn't get the robust version.

As for multi group analysis. The output is simply saying that you have to report the scaled/robust chi-square (find in the model output) and not the chi-square that is reported as part of multigroup testing. The warning is because you are trying to compare models with the same degrees of freedom - which is not possible.
Related to the mutli group analysis. In Model 5, although you include Pa ~  Be you still have the same degrees of freedom because you are replacing Pa ~~  Be. For measurement invariance, you are trying to test equality of factor loadings which you don't have (path analysis).

Hope this helps.

Best,
Jošt
